tools.name: list_directory
tools.description: List files and directories in a project-relative path. Use this to explore Source/ and Config/ directories. For finding Blueprints, Materials, Textures and other Unreal assets, prefer 'search_assets' instead — it searches the asset registry directly and is much faster than navigating directories manually. WARNING: NEVER use this tool to search for Unreal Engine assets (Blueprints, Materials, etc.). ALWAYS use the search_assets tool instead, which is significantly faster and more accurate.

directory.description: Project-relative directory path to list. Use empty string '' for project root. Examples: 'Source', 'Content/Blueprints', 'Config', 'Source/MyGame'

tools.name: search_assets
tools.description: Search the Unreal asset registry by name, class type, or path. Returns matching assets with their class and full content path. Use this FIRST when looking for Blueprints, Materials, Textures, Static Meshes, Skeletal Meshes, Animation assets, etc. This is MUCH faster than browsing directories with list_directory. CRITICAL: Use this tool FIRST to discover EXACT asset paths before calling tools like spawn_actor or set_component_properties.

query.description: Search term to match against asset names and paths (e.g. 'ThirdPerson', 'BP_Player', 'M_Rock')

tools.name: read_file_snippet
tools.description: Read a section of a source file with line numbers. Use this to inspect C++ headers, implementations, config files, or other text files. Supports .h, .cpp, .cs, .ini, .json, .txt, .xml, .yaml, .md, .py, .uplugin, .uproject files.

end_line.description: Last line to read (default: start_line + 99, max 500 lines per read)

tools.name: activate_skill
tools.description: Activate one or more lazy-loaded skill categories by adding them to the project's active_skills.json configuration.

skill_name.description: Name of the skill category to activate (e.g. 'animation', 'gas', 'pcg')

skills.description: Alternative array of skill names to activate

tools.name: enforce_naming_conventions
tools.description: Scan a content directory and enforce UE5 standard asset naming conventions (e.g. BP_ for Blueprints, SM_ for Static Meshes, M_ for Materials, T_ for Textures, WBP_ for Widgets). Renames non-conforming assets automatically or previews proposed renames when dry_run=true. Accepts parameter keys in both snake_case and PascalCase.

folder_path.description: Package directory path to scan for naming convention enforcement (e.g. '/Game/Blueprints', '/Game/UI', or '/Game/'). Accepts 'folder_path', 'directory_path', 'target_folder', or 'FolderPath'.

recursive.description: If true, recursively scan subdirectories. Default: true. Accepts 'recursive' or 'Recursive'.

dry_run.description: If true, evaluate naming conventions and return proposed renames without mutating assets. Default: false. Accepts 'dry_run', 'dry_run_mode', or 'DryRun'.

custom_rules.description: Optional mapping of asset class names to custom prefix strings (e.g. {"Blueprint": "BP_", "Texture2D": "T_"}). Accepts 'custom_rules' or 'CustomRules'.

tools.name: organize_assets_by_type
tools.description: Automatically reorganize mixed assets in a content folder into type-specific subdirectories (e.g., Blueprints/, Materials/, Textures/, Meshes/, Audio/, Effects/, UI/, Maps/). Supports preview mode via dry_run=true. Accepts parameter keys in both snake_case and PascalCase.

folder_path.description: Target content folder path to organize by asset class (e.g. '/Game/', '/Game/Imports'). Accepts 'folder_path', 'directory_path', 'source_path', or 'FolderPath'.

recursive.description: If true, recursively organize assets in subdirectories. Default: true. Accepts 'recursive' or 'Recursive'.

dry_run.description: If true, calculate proposed organization moves without executing asset relocations. Default: false. Accepts 'dry_run', 'dry_run_mode', or 'DryRun'.

create_subfolders.description: If true, automatically create missing type subfolders. Default: true. Accepts 'create_subfolders' or 'CreateSubfolders'.

tools.name: consolidate_asset_references
tools.description: Consolidate all references from a source asset to a target asset across the project and delete the source asset. Useful for merging duplicate assets or replacing deprecated references.

source_asset_path.description: Package path or object path of the source asset to replace and delete (e.g. '/Game/Materials/M_OldRock')

target_asset_path.description: Package path or object path of the target asset to replace references with (e.g. '/Game/Materials/M_Rock')

tools.name: delete_asset
tools.description: Delete an asset or package from the Unreal Engine project Content folder. Marks package for deletion, removes asset registry entry, and deletes the file from disk.

asset_path.description: Content package path or object path of the asset to delete (e.g. '/Game/AI/BT_Enemy' or '/Game/BP_TestActor')

tools.name: create_asset
tools.description: Universally create any new Unreal Engine asset by class name (e.g. 'NiagaraDataChannelAsset', 'NiagaraEffectType', 'InputMappingContext', 'InputAction', 'CurveFloat', 'CurveVector', 'CurveLinearColor', 'PhysicalMaterial', 'SoundCue', 'SoundAttenuation', 'MaterialParameterCollection', 'DataAsset', or any custom C++/Blueprint asset class). Dynamically discovers and instantiates the correct factory, or creates the package asset natively.

asset_path.description: Full content path for the new asset (e.g. '/Game/VFX/NDC_Impacts' or '/Game/Input/IMC_Default'). Alternatively provide package_path and asset_name.

package_path.description: Package folder path for the new asset (e.g. '/Game/VFX')

asset_name.description: Asset name for the new asset (e.g. 'NDC_Impacts')

asset_class.description: Class name of the asset to create (e.g. 'NiagaraDataChannelAsset', 'NiagaraEffectType', 'InputMappingContext', 'InputAction', 'PhysicalMaterial', 'CurveFloat', 'MaterialParameterCollection'). Aliases: class_name, ClassName, AssetClass.

factory_class.description: Optional specific factory class name to instantiate (e.g. 'NiagaraDataChannelAssetFactoryNew' or 'PhysicalMaterialFactoryNew'). If omitted, automatically discovered.
